sections.label: Singapore GDP and food production
sections.summary: Singapore is one of the richest countries by GDP per capita, producing high-value chips, pharmaceuticals and petroleum products, but produces less than 10% of its food.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Singapore is one of the richest countries in terms of gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, producing high-value semi-conductor chips, pharmaceuticals and petroleum products.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: But a basic necessity – food – we can only produce less than 10%.

sections.label: Food security and food waste
sections.summary: A country producing only 10% of its food is perceived as one of the most food-secure, yet throws away some 800,000 tonnes of food yearly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: As a result, a country which can lay claim to only 10% of its food production is perceived as one of the most food-secure countries in the world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: However, from the heights of this false security, we throw away some 800,000 tonnes of food every year.

sections.label: SFA redefined 30 by 30 goal
sections.summary: SFA redefined its original 2019 30 by 30 goal with targets of producing locally 20% greens and 30% seafood and eggs by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: SFA has recently redefined its original 30 by 30 goal announced in 2019 with more specific targets of producing locally – 20% greens and 30% seafood and eggs consumed by 2035.

sections.label: Singapore farms and food production
sections.summary: Six decades later, Singapore has less than 200 farms on 1% of its land, producing less than 10% of food consumed by six million people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Six decades later, we only have less than 200 farms, occupying 1% of our land and producing less than 10% of the food consumed by some six million people.

sections.label: Other countries food self-sufficiency rates
sections.summary: Food self-sufficiency rates are 50% in Japan, 54% in Switzerland, 60% in the United Kingdom and 65% in the Netherlands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: For instance, the self-sufficiency in food production rate in Japan is 50%; Switzerland is 54%; United Kingdom is 60%; and the Netherlands is 65%.

sections.label: Local food production as Total Defence
sections.summary: The Government is asked to consider local food production capability as part of Total Defence Security and to increase national Budget for it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider Local Food Production capability as part of our Total Defence Security?

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Just as we have spent billions of dollars over the past decades to build up our military defence capabilities, the Government may consider increasing our national Budget into building up our local food production capabilities.

sections.label: Climate warming and food production
sections.summary: Warming may affect food yields, so the speaker proposes reviewing increased Government support to boost local food production and self-sufficiency to at least 30%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: As the climate continues to warm, food production yields may also be massively affected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Hence, I propose that we review increasing Government support to boost our local food production and self-sufficiency rate to at least 30%.

sections.label: Singapore food waste statistics
sections.summary: Over five years, food waste averaged 790,000 tonnes yearly or 128 kilogrammes per capita, contributing 11% of total waste, with recycling around 18%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, food waste in Singapore averaged 790,000 tonnes per year or 128 kilogrammes per capita, and contributes to 11% of total waste.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The food recycling rate hovers at around 18%.

sections.label: D2L and IMPerfect Fellas initiatives
sections.summary: Since June 2023 D2L diverted 1,100 tonnes of food waste, while FairPrice Group's IMPerfect Fellas Initiative sells imperfect produce at a maximum of $2, diverting about 1,000 tonnes yearly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Since business launch in June 2023, D2L has diverted 1,100 tonnes of food waste.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: FairPrice Group had introduced the IMPerfect Fellas Initiative since 2015, to sell imperfect but edible fruits and vegetables bundled at a maximum of $2.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: This initiative diverts about 1,000 tonnes of produce from disposal every year.

sections.label: Food charities rescue food annually
sections.summary: Three food charities rescue about 2,400 tonnes of food annually, freeing incineration plant capacity; in 2025 Food Rescue Seng Kang diverted over 1,000 tonnes into 3.21 million meals for 312,000 families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Collectively, these three food charities rescue about 2,400 tonnes of food annually which frees up capacity at the incineration plants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: For instance, in 2025, Food Rescue Seng Kang diverted more than 1,000 tonnes of food from the incinerators and turned them into 3.21 million meals that served 312,000 families.

sections.label: Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill
sections.summary: Former MSE GPC Chairman Mr Louis Ng and the speaker worked with stakeholders and got the Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill passed in Parliament two years ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Former MSE GPC Chairman, Mr Louis Ng and I worked with numerous stakeholders and got the Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill passed in Parliament two years ago.

sections.label: Happy Lunch community dining pilot
sections.summary: The speaker started Happy Lunch @ Sembawang West, serving free healthy lunches to one hundred residents every Monday and Friday, and proposes a nationwide community-dining ecosystem supported by MSE, MOH and MSF.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: These community dining sessions are also opportunities for volunteers to engage the beneficiaries, as many seniors living alone suffer from loneliness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I recently started a small-scale pilot for community dining for residents, called Happy Lunch @ Sembawang West, with the support from grassroots volunteers and community partners, such as Food Rescue Seng Kang, and a few other food donors who care about food waste, food affordability, nutrition deficiency issues and are concerned about the vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Freshly prepared and healthy lunches are served free to one hundred residents, every Monday and Friday, at our Residents' Network Centre.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Happy Lunch is one example of how we can improve food sustainability and accessibility to affordable food, as well as strengthen emotional and physical health and community bonds, all at the same time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I propose that MSE, MOH and MSF jointly consider my proposal for a nationwide community-dining ecosystem and provide support to start more small-scale pilots across various towns.

sections.label: Motion on food resilience
sections.summary: The Motion calls on the Government to strengthen food resilience and mobilize society to reduce food waste so people can afford reasonably priced food despite geopolitical and climate risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Through this Motion, we are calling on the Government to strengthen food resilience and mobilize society to reduce food waste, making sure that people can still afford reasonably priced food despite geopolitical and climate risks.

sections.label: Supporting food charity organizations
sections.summary: The Government should support and recognize food charity organizations that rescue and redistribute over 2,000 tons of food yearly, helping those in need and encouraging less waste.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The Government should support and recognize food charity organizations that serve the community and rescue and redistribute over 2,000 tons of food each year, helping those in need spend less while encouraging the public to waste less food.

sections.label: Singapore Food Story 2
sections.summary: Singapore Food Story 2 broadens the approach to food resilience as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Singapore Food Story 2 broadens our approach to food resilience as a whole.

sections.label: Changed circumstances since 2019 goal
sections.summary: An aspirational goal based on nutritional needs was set in 2019, but circumstances have changed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While we had in 2019 set up an aspirational goal based on nutritional needs, circumstances have changed.

sections.label: Monitoring imported input reliance
sections.summary: The question asks how the Government monitors local food production's reliance on imported seed, feed, fertiliser and energy, and whether input dependency concentration is assessed and factored into production targets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Alongside production volumes and number of sources, I would like to ask the Government how we monitor local food production's reliance on imported inputs, including seed, feed, fertiliser and energy, whether the concentration of these input dependencies is assessed and how this is factored into our local production targets.

sections.label: 30 by 30 farm yield estimates
sections.summary: When 30 by 30 was developed, the Government estimated an average vegetable farm produced about 130 tonnes per hectare yearly, while a high-tech farm could produce over 1,000 tonnes per hectare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: When 30 by 30 was developed, the Government estimated that an average vegetable farm in Singapore produced approximately 130 tonnes per hectare each year, whereas a high-tech farm could potentially produce more than 1,000 tonnes per hectare.

sections.label: Green Harvest hydroponic glass greenhouse farm
sections.summary: Green Harvest is a two-hectare farm with a large automated hydroponic glass greenhouse system producing up to 4,000kg of leafy vegetables a day.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Green Harvest is a two-hectare farm with a large automated hydroponic glass greenhouse system, producing up to 4,000kg of leafy vegetables a day.

sections.label: Lim Chu Kang farms affected by conversion
sections.summary: In 2014, 62 farms in Lim Chu Kang were affected by plans to convert farmland for military training, as defence land elsewhere was released for Tengah.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2014, 62 farms in Lim Chu Kang were affected by plans to convert farmland for military training, as defence land elsewhere was released for Tengah.

sections.label: Lim Chu Kang land re-allocation
sections.summary: Jurong Frog Farm returned its Lim Chu Kang site, and this year the Government announced northern Lim Chu Kang defence land will be re-allocated for future agriculture while southern agricultural land will be re-purposed for defence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Jurong Frog Farm also returned its Lim Chu Kang site.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This year, Government announced that land in northern Lim Chu Kang currently designated for defence will instead be re-allocated for future agriculture, while agricultural land in southern Lim Chu Kang will eventually be re-purposed for defence.

sections.label: Interim farm use and masterplan update
sections.summary: Some southern Lim Chu Kang tenures expire in 2026 and 2027, reinstatement works for future defence use may begin only from 2030, and the speaker asks for a clearer interim farm use framework and updates on the Lim Chu Kang masterplan and Agri-Food Innovation Park.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Some southern Lim Chu Kang tenures expire soon in 2026 and 2027, while I understand that necessary reinstatement works for the future defence use may begin only from 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Where land has been designated for a future use whose works begin sometime later, could there be a clearer framework for interim farm use, rather than leaving it unused?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask for an update of the overall Lim Chu Kang masterplan and the Agri-Food Innovation Park.

sections.label: Agriculture graduates and food imports
sections.summary: The passage asks how many graduates from these programmes eventually enter the agriculture sector, noting that today more than 90% of food is imported from overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How many graduates from these programmes eventually enter the agriculture sector?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Today, more than 90% of our food is imported from overseas.

sections.label: Cheng San community garden food programme
sections.summary: A Residents' Network in Cheng San running a community garden has started designing a Little Food Heroes programme on growing goodness, exposing younger children to food security concepts and activities such as composting, as Singapore prepares to chair ASEAN in 2027.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To this end, one of our Residents' Network in Cheng San which also runs a community garden with an active harvest, has started designing a Little Food Heroes programme about growing goodness, exposing younger children to food security concepts and letting them experience activities, such as composting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As Singapore prepares to chair the ASEAN in 2027, practical regional food resilience can be a meaningful priority for our region.

sections.label: Agri-food pilots with neighbours
sections.summary: Asks whether Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia could explore mutually beneficial agri-food pilots in climate-resilient production, cold-chain, research and green lanes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Could Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia, for example, explore a small number of mutually beneficial agri-food pilots in climate-resilient production, cold-chain solutions, research and demonstration or green lanes for more efficient movement of time-sensitive food where regulatory requirements are met?

sections.label: Grow Local technology and land
sections.summary: States Grow Local must embrace technology, pursue productivity without losing diversity, and make land choices remembering farms, people and knowledge take time to build.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Grow Local must embrace technology without putting all our eggs in the same basket, pursue productivity without losing diversity and make difficult land choices without forgetting that farms, people and knowledge take time to build, and they are much harder to recreate once they are gone.

sections.label: Singapore Food Story 2 targets
sections.summary: States local production complements diversification, and the Government shifted to Singapore Food Story 2 targets of 20% fibre and 30% protein by 2035, with research, technology and grant funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Boosting local food production does not replace diversification, but it is a critical complement to add a layer to food security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This year, the Government has shifted targets from "30 by 30" by introducing the Singapore Food Story 2 – 20% of our fibre and 30% of our protein to be locally produced by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: To be fair, the Government has invested a $309 million research fund, a $60 million technology transformation fund and 39.4 million in express grants to help farmers produce food.

sections.label: Surveys on buying local produce
sections.summary: States SFA's 2020 survey found 94% willing to buy local produce but only 65% could identify it, and a 2024 YouGov survey found up to 59% neutral.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Singapore Food Agency's (SFA's) survey in 2020 found that 94% of Singaporeans were willing to buy local produce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Yet only 65% could even identify it when shopping.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: A YouGov survey in 2024 found that up to 59% of shoppers were simply neutral – not opposed to buying local, just without a reason to choose it over the cheaper import beside it on the shelf.

sections.label: FairPrice delisting local vegetables
sections.summary: States FairPrice, with around 160 outlets, will delist locally grown vegetables from at least three farms as part of a category assortment refresh.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Recently, we saw the starkest illustration yet when FairPrice, our largest retailer with around 160 outlets, will delist locally grown vegetables from at least three farms – Artisan Green, Sg Veg Farms and Netafarm – as part of a category assortment refresh.

sections.label: France AMAP and guaranteed offtake
sections.summary: Describes France's AMAP network growth and proposes guaranteed offtake requiring supermarket chains and SAF cookhouses to source a minimum share of fresh produce locally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: France's AMAP network, an association for the maintenance of small-holder agriculture, started with a handful of consumer groups and now spans over 2,000 associations serving 320 consumers across 3,500 farms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Second, to guaranteed offtake for farmers by requiring our largest supermarket chains and SAF cookhouses to source a guaranteed minimum share of their fresh produce from local farms.

sections.label: Brazil local farmer meal purchases
sections.summary: Brazilian federal law requires at least 30% of school meal spending to go to local family farmers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In Brazil, federal law mandates that at least 30% of school meal expenditure must go to purchases from local family farmers.

sections.label: New York local food sourcing
sections.summary: A 2023 executive order directs New York state agencies to source 30% of food from local farmers by 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In New York, an executive order signed in 2023 directs state agencies to source 30% of their food from local farmers by 2027.

sections.label: Fibre and protein production cost
sections.summary: At current production levels, eight percent of fibre and 26% of protein, the physical cost is likely modest relative to GST collections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: At current production levels, eight percent of fibre and 26% of protein, the physical cost is likely to be modest relative to overall GST collections.

sections.label: Farm tax measures and Ireland
sections.summary: Reduced corporate tax, capital allowances and energy deductions would lower production costs, and Ireland applies reduced farming income tax and stock relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: A reduced corporate tax rate for qualifying farms, enhanced capital allowances for agricultural equipment, or deductions for energy cost will lower the cost of production and to further close the price gap from the supply side.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Among those, Ireland applies reduced income tax rate to farming income and offers stock relief, 25% deduction on the increased value of livestock and produce.

sections.label: Income averaging in other jurisdictions
sections.summary: Variants of income averaging or smoothing mechanisms already exist in the US, UK, France and the Netherlands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Variants of income averaging or income smoothing mechanisms already exist in jurisdictions such as the US, the UK, France and the Netherlands.

sections.label: Half revised fibre target vegetables
sections.summary: Reaching half the revised fibre target, 10% instead of 20%, is roughly 50,000 tonnes of vegetables yearly that no export ban, shipping disruption or foreign government can touch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: If we reach even half the revised fibre target, 10% locally produced instead of 20%, that is roughly half the total.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: That is roughly 50,000 tonnes of vegetables grown here every year that no export ban can touch, no shipping disruption can delay, and no foreign government can withhold.

sections.label: Diversifying Singapore food sources
sections.summary: Singapore diversified food sources, sourcing from more than 180 countries and regions in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Singapore’s strategy of diversifying our food sources is the right one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We sourced food from more than 180 countries and regions in 2025.

sections.label: Singapore-New Zealand essential supplies agreement
sections.summary: The Singapore-New Zealand Agreement on Trade in Essential Supplies sets commitments on export restrictions, movement of goods, information-sharing and consultation during disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The question should not only be: “Can this country supply us with food?” It should also be: “What options does this partnership give us when normal supply chains are disrupted?” The Singapore-New Zealand Agreement on Trade in Essential Supplies is an interesting example.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: It establishes commitments around keeping essential supplies flowing during disruptions, including on export restrictions, movement of goods, information-sharing and consultation.

sections.label: Food Pact with Australia
sections.summary: The Food Pact with Australia covers food trade and innovation, inspection system recognition, disease regionalisation and a simplified transhipment model for Australian red meat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Our Food Pact with Australia is an interesting example of this broader approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: It includes cooperation on food trade and innovation, but also areas such as recognition of inspection systems, disease regionalisation and a simplified transhipment model for Australian red meat.

sections.label: Singapore food waste and recycling
sections.summary: Singapore generated about 790,000 tonnes of food waste in 2025, with a food recycling rate of around 18 percent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Singapore generated about 790,000 tonnes of food waste in 2025, with a food recycling rate of around 18 percent.

sections.label: Food rescue groups' 2025 figures
sections.summary: Sengkang Food Rescue rescued over 1,000 tonnes of food in 2025, and Fridge Restock Community completed 500 food rescues by December last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Sengkang Food Rescue shared that they have rescued more than 1,000 tonnes of food in 2025, which it estimated was equivalent to the needs of around 312,000 families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Fridge Restock Community similarly shared that they have completed 500 food rescues as of December last year.

sections.label: Land for community food-rescue storage
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government can work with agencies to identify land or spaces for community food-rescue storage supporting existing rescue networks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Could the Government work with the relevant agencies to identify suitable land or spaces that could be used for community food-rescue storage, particularly where these can support existing rescue networks?

sections.label: Storage as food rescue
sections.summary: Reducing food waste requires recognising that storage is part of food rescue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Because if we are serious about reducing food waste, we need to recognise that storage is part of food rescue.

sections.label: Food rescue and resilience
sections.summary: Food rescue should be recognised as part of food resilience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Second, let us recognise that food rescue is part of food resilience.

sections.label: Singapore local food production
sections.summary: Singapore produces about a third of eggs and 3% of vegetables, with the 30 by 30 target dropped.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, Singapore produces about a third of all eggs consumed and 3% of vegetable consumed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Local production meets about 8% of our fibre consumption and 25% of our protein consumption as of 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our initial "30 by 30" target to produce 30% of Singapore's nutritional needs by 2030 was dropped last year amid failing local food production over the years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While egg production increased impressively, vegetable production fell from 23,500 tonnes in 2021 to 16,600 tonnes in 2025; while seafood production fell from 5,100 tonnes in 2021 to 3,800 tonnes in 2025.

sections.label: Longer agricultural land leases
sections.summary: The Government is asked to consider tendering agricultural land on longer leases tied to production targets and reviews.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Government consider tendering out agricultural land on longer leases of 30 years or 20+20 years, provided that these leases are tied to clear production targets and periodic reviews to ensure that the farmers are meeting KPIs?

sections.label: Singapore food re-exports
sections.summary: Singapore's 2025 re-exports of fish, seafood, vegetables and fruit totalled about $520 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2025, Singapore re-exports of fish, seafood, vegetables and fruit amounted to some $520 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This figure appears quite small compared to other food transshipment hubs, such as the Netherlands, which is the primary re-export hub for fresh fruits and vegetables for Europe through the port of Rotterdam, and re-exported agricultural products with a value of €49 billion in 2025.

sections.label: Singapore food manufacturing sector
sections.summary: As of 2024, Singapore's food manufacturing sector has over 1,500 companies, 68,000 workers and about 1% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As of 2024, Singapore's food manufacturing sector comprises over 1,500 companies, employing around 68,000 workers and contributing about 1% of GDP.

sections.label: Singapore food waste tonnes
sections.summary: In 2025, almost 800,000 tonnes of food waste were generated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2025, we generated almost 800,000 tonnes of food waste.

sections.label: Government support for food initiatives
sections.summary: The Government can provide grants and logistical support, and a centralised platform linking food businesses with food rescue charities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government can do more to support by providing financial grants and logistical support to encourage the growth of more of these ground-up initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A Government-run centralised platform connecting local food businesses directly with neighbourhood food rescue charities could also help ensure that excess food reaches those who need it more rapidly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It reduces our carbon footprint and provides immediate dignity preserving relief to Singaporeans highest hit by the rising cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To ensure every Singapore family has affordable food on the table, regardless of external crisis, we must give our farmers the land stability they need to innovate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We expand our role as a food manufacturing, processing, trading and transshipment hub, and build robust public-civil partnerships to eliminate food waste.

sections.label: Cavendish banana disease vulnerability
sections.summary: Traded bananas are almost all Cavendish, genetically similar and vulnerable to TR4, which is detected in many producing countries.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Bananas are grown across Asia, Latin America and Africa, and importers sourcing from several countries may therefore appear well diversified, but almost all bananas traded internationally are Cavendish.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Cavendish plants are genetically very similar, and that uniformity leaves the traded banana supply particularly vulnerable to diseases such as tropical race four (TR4).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: TR4 has now been detected in many banana producing countries, while a large proportion of global banana production remains susceptible.

sections.label: Food security resilience testing
sections.summary: Scenarios used in food security exercises have been published, and modelling assesses calorie supply and nutrition under disruption.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What can we say publicly about how that resilience is actually tested?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It has published some of the scenarios used in its food security exercises, including substantial simultaneous reductions in imports of major grains.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Its Ministry of Agriculture is also developing modelling that combines production, imports, stocks and global supply conditions to assess calorie supply and nutritional balance under disruption.

sections.label: Links to alternative sources
sections.summary: First, usable links to alternative sources are needed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, we need usable links to alternative sources.

sections.label: Network financial reconfiguration capacity
sections.summary: The network also needs financial capacity to reconfigure itself.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The network also needs financial capacity to reconfigure itself.

sections.label: Flexible demand shifting
sections.summary: Adaptability also depends on how flexibly demand can shift.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, adaptability also depends on how flexibly demand can shift.

sections.label: Assessing agri-food investments
sections.summary: Selected agri-food investments should be assessed on commercial case and contribution to Singapore's food resilience.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The additional consideration I propose is straightforward for selected agri-food investments assess not only the commercial case, but the enterprises contribution to Singapore's food resilience.

sections.label: Double dividend from approach
sections.summary: Done well, the approach can deliver stronger food resilience and stronger Singapore agri-food SMEs able to scale regionally and globally.

sentences.text: Done well, this approach can deliver a double dividend, a stronger food resilience, stronger Singapore agri-food SMEs with the networks and capabilities to scale regionally and globally.

sentences.text: The last time our statistics were reported on their own was in 2024, when locally farmed seafood was 6.1% of what we ate, down from 7.3%, and 7.6% the years before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Behind that falling share, the number of farms is falling too: 98 sea-based fish farms in 2023, to 72, to 67 in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Today it fetches around $7, half the price, while wages have tripled and feed has risen 80%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A local seabass costs more to grow than an imported one costs to buy, around $7.80 against $6 at the wet market.

sections.label: Shared multi-tenanted farm facilities
sections.summary: Under Food Story 2, the Government is studying shared, multi-tenanted facilities to lower production costs for vegetable and agritech farms.

sentences.text: Because lose these farms, we do not just lose 6.1% of our self-sufficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But there is also a "soft" half: living coral reefs and breeding grounds that protect our coastline, and these already exist within our fish farms.

sections.label: Helping fish farmers

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, help fish farmers process their produce, add value and secure reliable buyers.

sections.label: Food insecurity prevalence data
sections.summary: Reports estimate about 10% of Singaporean households face food insecurity, with FAO finding 9.5% affected in 2022 to 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The 2019 Hunger Report, now more than six years old, estimated that around 10% of Singaporean households face food insecurity.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The United Nations (UN) Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), covering the period 2022 to 2024, found that 9.5% of our population, over 500,000 people, experience moderate to severe food insecurity, with 3.5% experiencing severe food insecurity, meaning insufficient food quantity and risk of physical hunger.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This report found that prevalence has tripled comparing 2014 to 2016 against 2022 to 2024.

sections.label: Singapore Food Story 2 targets

sentences.text: For example, research on food insecure pregnant women at KK Women's and Children's Hospital published just last year, found that food insecure pregnant women often present with higher than average body weight, while suffering real deficiencies in the form of low haemoglobin and Vitamin D.

sections.label: Food insecurity support and data
sections.summary: Notes only 22% of food insecure households received support and calls for a fresh national study and harmonised eligibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Here in Singapore, it is worth noting that the Hunger Report found that only 22% of food insecure households received support.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Of those, only one in five felt it made a lasting difference, suggesting that the problem is extremely complex.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We must also ask whether every household, especially those least visible to us, can reliably access and afford it, in good times as well as bad.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We need a fresh, nationally representative study updating the 2019 Hunger Report, so this House is no longer relying on old data for a problem that the FAO tells us has multiplied over the years.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Any review of support schemes must also begin with harmonising eligibility across ComCare, Food Banks and community assistance, so access does not depend on which door a struggling family happens to knock on.

sections.label: NEA-managed hawker centres

sentences.text: And after more than a decade, the Government's own data appears to show that occupancy, store turnover, satisfaction and even rents appear to be broadly comparable between SEHC and NEA-managed centres.

sentences.text: NEA can retain the direct relationship with our hawkers and build up its own institutional expertise, rather than assuming that professional management necessarily requires a middle man in the form of a master tenant.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But ask any household doing their grocery run, and the reality is this: local produce still costs around 30% more than the imported alternative.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Despite schemes, like the SG Fresh Produce logo, local vegetable and seafood consumption has continued to decline.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: FairPrice also recently pulled produce from at least three local farms off its shelves even as our farmers contend with rising costs that only widened the price gap.

sections.label: Urban farms wholesale deals

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In July, seven urban farms struck wholesale deals with buyers like SATS and central kitchens, which is worth scaling.

sections.label: Closed eateries outside scheme
sections.summary: Ka-Soh and Wing Seong Fatty's closed for reasons like no successor and no institutional bridge, but fall outside the scheme as they are not Government managed.

sentences.text: Ka-Soh and Wing Seong Fatty's closed for the same reasons many hawker stalls once did – no successor, no institutional bridge – but they fall outside the scheme purely because they are not Government managed.

sentences.text: Ms Poh, you have a clarification to make?

sentences.text: I misspoke that D2L.sg diverted 1,100 tonnes of food waste since the business launched in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: It should be 1,100 tonnes of food waste in 2025 alone.

sentences.text: Meals at hawker centres, coffee shops and food courts account for the largest share of food and beverage services expenses at 50.8%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: NEA has confirmed it does not regulate cooked food prices directly, relying instead on tender conditions to provide budget meals.

sections.label: Singapore food import vulnerability
sections.summary: Singapore imports over 90% of its food, and successive shocks will keep testing this vulnerability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Singapore imports over 90% of our food and successive shocks – the pandemic, the Ukraine conflict's fertiliser disruptions, and now the Middle East crisis – will keep testing this vulnerability.

sections.label: Agri-food facilities and subsidies
sections.summary: The Government is urged to build multi-tenanted agri-food production facilities and provide subsidies to keep rents manageable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To deal with the high costs, I urge the Government to take immediate steps to execute a plan to build multi-tenanted facilities for agri-food production and ensure that subsidies are in place to keep rents manageable as they grow.

sections.label: Hawker meal vouchers and farmers
sections.summary: A targeted Hawker Meal Voucher scheme is proposed, and support for local farmers in lease tenures, technology and research is urged.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This can be seen as an extension of the budget meals scheme at socially conscious enterprise hawker centres, so that this scheme can be rolled out to all hawker centres and benefit more low-income Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I would like us to consider a targeted "Hawker Meal Voucher" scheme ring-fenced within existing Community Development Council (CDC) Voucher allocations, redeemable specifically at budget-meal stalls, for households identified through existing ComCare, Public Assistance and HDB rental flat schemes to deliver targeted support for our lower-income households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The JB-SG Rapid Transit System is expected to put pressure on our merchants and hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We need to ensure that these affordable and accessible food options remain available to our lower income groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin): I hope that we have not missed the boat on supporting our local farmers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This, together with stronger food waste partnerships and structural hawker affordability measures, is how we deliver on the Motion's call for a food system that is resilient, low-waste and genuinely affordable for every household.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Support for our local farmers, particularly in lease tenures, technology and research, will be crucial to help them develop and sustain their businesses.

sections.label: Food resilience as structural priority
sections.summary: The Government is urged to treat food resilience, waste reduction and affordability as one structural priority rather than separate cost-of-living cushions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Support for our local farmers, particularly in lease tenures, technology and research, will be crucial to help them develop and sustain their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to treat food resilience, waste reduction and affordability not as separate cost-of-living cushions to be topped up at each Budget cycle, but as one structural priority, so that when prices rise, it is the burden that is shared, and it is surplus that is redirected.

sections.label: 30 by 30 goal replaced
sections.summary: In November 2025 the Government replaced the 30 by 30 goal with 2035 targets of 20 percent fibre and 30 percent protein.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In November 2025, the Government replaced our national commitment to produce 30% of our nutritional needs locally by 2030, known as the "30 by 30" goal, with revised 2035 targets of 20 percent for fibre and 30 percent for protein, citing pandemic supply shocks, high energy and manpower cost, and tough financing conditions.

sections.label: Local vegetable and seafood consumption
sections.summary: SFA's June 2025 report states locally farmed vegetables were three percent of consumption and local seafood 6.1 percent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the SFA's Singapore Food Statistics report released in June 2025, locally farmed vegetables accounted for just three percent of total domestic consumption, while local seafood dropped to 6.1%.

sections.label: Caterers meeting farm-to-table threshold
sections.summary: Caterers can meet SFA's 15 percent farm to table threshold by buying low-cost items already at price parity, like eggs or bean sprouts, bypassing local leafy greens and fish.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, caterers can meet SFA's 15 percent farm to table threshold by buying low-cost items that already have price parity, like eggs or bean sprouts, completely bypassing local leafy greens and fish.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Specifically, they should set an institutional baseline of 35% for protein across seafood and eggs, and 25% for fibre via vegetables within their catering budgets.

sentences.text: To ensure compliance with Singapore's Free Trade Agreements and the World Trade Organization's Government Procurement Agreements, which generally prohibit discriminatory non-tariff barriers, the Government can utilise perfectly legal work arounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Across our major institutional buyers, including army camps, about 12,000 public hospital beds and 6,500 individuals in our prison facilities, total catering contracts across these core domains conservatively exceed $300 million annually.

sections.label: Cost of demand-side rebate
sections.summary: Under proposed targets of 25% fibre and 35% protein, caterers would procure about $23 million to $32 million of SG Certified local produce annually, with a 25% cashback rebate costing Government $6 million to $8 million annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under my proposed institutional targets of 25% for fibre and 35% for protein, caterers would procure approximately $23 million to $32 million worth of SG Certified local produce annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Applying a 25% cashback rebate strictly to this local offtake brings the total cost to the Government to between $6 million and $8 million annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This modest annual expenditure stands in stark contrast to supply side interventions like the initial $60 million Agri-food Cluster Transformation Fund and its subsequent $70 million top-up, which averages roughly $14 million annually over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Re-allocating or matching even a fraction of this capital into a targeted demand side rebate guarantees immediate offtake revenue for our local farms and would be vastly more capital efficient than repeatedly pouring tens of millions of dollars into supply side grant for infrastructure that risks sitting under-utilised without guaranteed buyers.

sentences.text: The Act can be amended to allow food past its quality date mark to be donated.

sentences.text: In 2016, NEA found that food made up half the waste of Singapore households and half of that was avoidable.

sections.label: Diversifying food import sources
sections.summary: Diversification gives alternative sources, with a network of over 20 sources including Thailand, Vietnam, India, Japan and the US.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Diversification ensures that we have alternative sources to turn to and we have worked closely with the industry over the years to build an extensive network of over 20 sources, including Thailand, Vietnam, India, Japan and the US.

sections.label: Refreshed local production targets
sections.summary: Local production targets were refreshed to supply 20% of fibre and 30% of protein consumption by 2035.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Drawing on the lessons of the past six years, we had refreshed our local production targets to build the capability and capacity of local farms to supply 20% of local consumption of fibre and 30% of local consumption of protein by 2035.

sections.label: Funding and farm productivity gains
sections.summary: Over $240 million was set aside since 2019, with productivity rising for vegetable, seafood and egg farms from 2019 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Since 2019, we have set aside more than $240 million to support local production.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: From 2019 to 2025, the productivity rose by 20% for vegetable farms, 46% for seafood farms and 40% for egg farms.

sections.label: SFA awards to farm projects
sections.summary: SFA has awarded close to $60 million to over 160 projects supporting various farms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: To date, SFA has awarded close to $60 million to over 160 projects, supporting a wide range of farms from open cage to closed containment fish farms, and from traditional soil-based to urban indoor vegetable farms.

sections.label: Agri-food Cluster Transformation Fund 2
sections.summary: An additional $70 million under Agri-food Cluster Transformation Fund 2 supports farms in technology adoption and capability-building.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: With the additional $70 million under Agri-food Cluster Transformation Fund 2 announced in March, farms can look forward to continued support for technology adoption and capability-building.

sections.label: Farm Business Resilience Support grant
sections.summary: A one-off Farm Business Resilience Support grant was introduced in July to help local farms with cost pressures from the Middle East conflict.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In July, we introduced the one-off Farm Business Resilience Support grant to help local farms deal with the cost pressures from the Middle East conflict.

sections.label: Singapore Food R&D Programme funding
sections.summary: More than $110 million under the Singapore Food R&D Programme funds research into agriculture and aquaculture inputs and farming solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: More than $110 million has been made available under the Singapore Food R&D Programme, for research into better agriculture and aquaculture inputs and farming solutions that can help improve the economics of production.

sections.label: pH optimisation research yield improvement
sections.summary: Research on pH optimisation gave a 10% yield improvement, and findings were shared with hydroponics farms ComCrop and CropCiti.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Research on pH optimisation similarly delivered a 10% improvement in yield, and findings have since been shared with hydroponics farms such as ComCrop and CropCiti.

sections.label: Alternative protein R&D funding
sections.summary: Across RIE2020 and RIE2025, over 50 alternative protein projects received about $130 million in R&D funding.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Across the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2020 (RIE2020) and RIE2025, the Government has supported more than 50 alternative protein projects with about $130 million in R&D funding.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For cell-based proteins, this includes work on reducing production costs and scaling up manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For plant-based proteins, this includes work on improving nutrition, taste, and texture.

sections.label: Lim Chu Kang Masterplan and land swap
sections.summary: The Lim Chu Kang Masterplan and Agri-Food Innovation Park advance through inter-agency planning and studies, with a proposed MINDEF land swap.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: So, we have done that for many years after the expiration of the lease, and now I think this is a time where we really need to re-arrange and re-organise our land and have a land swap with MINDEF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We are continuing to advance the Lim Chu Kang Masterplan and Agri-Food Innovation Park through inter-agency planning and detailed studies on land-use optimisation, infrastructure requirements, and environmental considerations.

sections.label: SAFEF agreements with vegetable suppliers
sections.summary: SAFEF signed new Memoranda of Understanding with local vegetable suppliers serving institutional buyers, contributing to more stable demand for farmers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In July, SAFEF signed new Memoranda of Understanding with local vegetable suppliers serving institutional buyers and this contributes to more stable demand for our farmers as our Members here have suggested.

sections.label: No mandated sourcing for buyers
sections.summary: Buyers must balance affordability, supply consistency, quality and preferences, so sourcing is not mandated; instead farms are helped to aggregate supply and match larger buyers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: While we encourage all buyers to consider local produce in their sourcing mix, buyers, such as supermarkets and caterers, need to balance considerations of affordability, consistency of supply, food quality and consumer preferences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Our approach is therefore not to mandate sourcing requirements, as this may inadvertently reduce access to more affordable sources of food and increase costs of business and consumers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Instead, we focus on helping local farms become more competitive and reliable suppliers by aggregating their supply and matching them with larger and more stable buyers.

sections.label: Long-term food price pressures
sections.summary: Upward pressure on food prices is likely to persist due to climate change, disease outbreaks, geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions, which the Singapore Food Story 2 can help manage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Over the longer term, upward pressure on food prices is likely to persist.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Climate change, disease outbreaks, geopolitical tensions and disruptions to supply chains can affect agricultural yields and raise the cost of producing and moving food.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We cannot fully insulate Singapore from these global pressures, but through our Singapore Food Story 2, we can better manage the impact of disruptions on our food supply.

sections.label: Three considerations guiding food strategy
sections.summary: The Government is guided by three main considerations in formulating this food resilience strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In formulating this food resilience strategy, the Government is guided by three main considerations.

sections.label: Four-pronged food resilience approach
sections.summary: The Government adopts a four-pronged approach of diversifying imports, stockpiling, enhancing local production and deepening global partnerships, with SFA funding and R&D investment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Singapore cannot fully insulate itself from these external pressures, but the Government will strengthen our ability to respond to risks and shocks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We are adopting a four-pronged approach: diversifying imports, stockpiling, enhancing local food production and deepening global partnerships to strengthen our food resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: To date, SFA has awarded close to $60 million through the Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund to support more than 160 projects, with a further $70 million committed to support the next phase of innovation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: At the same time, the Government has invested more than $100 million in food R&D programmes to translate research outcomes into practical farming solutions and improve productivity and resource efficiency.

sections.label: Commitment to available affordable food
sections.summary: The commitment remains to ensure food supplies remain available, assured and affordable regardless of external circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: No matter how external circumstances evolve, our commitment remains the same: to ensure food supplies remain available, assured and affordable.

sections.label: Farm offtake and local fish labelling
sections.summary: A member clarifies that farmers may sell to other channels, and another says SFA struggles to distinguish local fish from imported fish sold as local.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Giam, you have a clarification to make.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: She said that, regarding farm offtake, it is for SAFEF to find the most optimal channel for their business and to produce solely to the public sector will deprive them of selling to the best segment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: I was asking the Government to buy much more from local farmers to guarantee greater offtake of their farm produce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Farmers can and should continue to sell to other channels, including supermarkets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Tiong, you have a clarification to ask?

sentences.text: I have been to multiple local fish farms, and one of the common criticisms is that SFA does not seem to easily distinguish between fish grown and produced in Singapore farms, versus fish that are imported, held briefly and then sold as local.

sections.label: SAFEF aquaculture farm registration
sections.summary: Only 23 of the 67 remaining aquaculture farms are registered with SAFEF, and the member asks for SFA's strategies to attract more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou
sentences.text: From what I understand on SAFEF, there is only 23 aquaculture farms registered out of the 67 that currently remain, so I am just wondering what are some strategies that SFA has to convince more farmers to come on board to SAFEF.

sections.label: Singapore food imports
sections.summary: Singapore imports more than 90% of its food.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: Singapore imports more than 90% of our food.

sections.label: Temporary cost of living support
sections.summary: Temporary support for higher living costs includes CDC Vouchers, the Enhanced Budget 2026 Cost of Living Special Payment and additional U-Save rebates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: First, we provide temporary support to help Singaporeans with higher living costs, such as through CDC Vouchers, the Enhanced Budget 2026 Cost of Living Special Payment and additional U-Save rebates.

sections.label: CDC meal initiatives
sections.summary: North West CDC's food vending machines provide $3 meals, and North East CDC's Warm Meals initiative delivers free warm meals via food lockers near rental flats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: For example, North West CDC's food vending machines provides $3 meals, while North East CDC's Warm Meals initiative delivers free warm meals through food lockers near rental flat residents.

sections.label: Hawker Centres Upgrading Programme 2.0
sections.summary: Announced at last year's Committee of Supply debates, the Hawker Centres Upgrading Programme 2.0 will invest in existing hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: In addition, as announced at the Committee of Supply debates last year, we will invest in our existing hawker centres through the Hawker Centres Upgrading Programme 2.0, so that they continue serving the needs of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Hawker stallholder support package
sections.summary: The Government announced a six-month support package for stallholders at hawker centres and markets to offset rental costs and ease cost pressures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: The Government has therefore announced a six-month support package for stallholders at hawker centres and markets to help offset rental costs and ease cost pressures.

sections.label: Hawker manpower and rent policies
sections.summary: NEA allows LTVP or LTVP+ holders with Letters of Consent to work as stall assistants since 2025, and keeps hawker centre rents stable, with median rent around $1,250 monthly for a decade.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: On manpower, NEA has opened up manpower access by allowing Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) or LTVP Plus (LTVP+) holders with Letters of Consent to work as stall assistants since 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: On rents, NEA has policies in place to keep rents at hawker centres stable, including implementing cooling measures since 2024 to deter excessively high stall tender bids.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: The median rent for non-subsidised cooked food stallholders has remained relatively stable at around $1,250 per month for the last decade or so.

sections.label: SEHC rental caps and reinvestment
sections.summary: To safeguard SEHCs' social mission, stall rentals are capped at the average independently assessed market rent, and operators must reinvest at least 50% of any operating surplus into the hawker centre.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: At the same time, to safeguard the social mission of SEHCs, stall rentals are capped at the average independently assessed market rent, and operators must reinvest at least 50% of any operating surplus into the hawker centre.

sections.label: Singapore food waste generated 2025
sections.summary: In 2025, Singapore generated 790,000 tonnes of food waste, about 11% of total waste generated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: In 2025, we generated 790,000 tonnes of food waste, accounting for about 11% of total waste generated in Singapore.

sections.summary: Since it was passed in 2024, the Act has created a more enabling environment for food redistribution by protecting food donors from liability if specific safety conditions are met.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: Since it was passed in 2024, the Act has created a more enabling environment for food redistribution by protecting food donors from liability if specific safety conditions are met.

sections.label: SFA study on date-mark donations
sections.summary: SFA is embarking on a study to assess the safety and feasibility of allowing food that has passed quality-based date-marks to be donated, while maintaining food safety standards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: SFA is thus embarking on a study to assess the safety and feasibility of allowing food that has passed quality-based date-marks to be donated, while maintaining food safety standards at the same time.

sections.label: Food waste co-digestion facility
sections.summary: A facility will co-digest food waste with used water sludge, starting second half of 2028, treating up to 400 tonnes daily.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: The facility will co-digest food waste with used water sludge to recover energy, allowing us to extract more value from food waste than through incineration alone.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: This facility is expected to commence operations in the second half of 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: When fully operational, it will be able to treat up to 400 tonnes of food waste per day, representing approximately 18% of Singapore’s annual food waste generated.

sections.label: NEA food waste funding
sections.summary: NEA's 3R Fund supported about 30 food waste treatment projects with $2.4 million, and the Closing the Resource Loop Fund committed $5.3 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: NEA's 3R Fund has supported around 30 food waste treatment projects with approximately $2.4 million in funding, while the Closing the Resource Loop Fund has committed around $5.3 million to food waste valorisation projects.

sections.label: Government food resilience duties
sections.summary: It sets out duties for the Government on accessible affordable food, local production, and coordinated import and redistribution policy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: First, it paints a duty for the Government to ensure that food supply remains always accessible and affordable for Singaporeans, factoring in disruptions due to geopolitical conflicts and extreme climate events.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Second, it reminds us that food resilience requires building up local food production capability and viability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Third, it requires the Government to design a more coordinated food import policy and food redistribution ecosystem, to reduce food waste at the systems level, so that we can have a robust infrastructure and strategy for the long term.

sections.label: Supporting local and alternative food
sections.summary: It asks Singaporeans to support local farmers and Grow in SG produce, and to accept alternative proteins for food resilience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: We must be creative about unlocking the hidden potential in unsold and rescued food, turn them into nutritious meals, and in so doing reduce food waste.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: We ask Singaporeans to support our local farmers and buy Grow in SG local produce, even if the vegetables, fish and eggs may cost more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Our local farmers have to transform their operations and scale up production in order to stay competitive, to overcome tight land, water, energy and manpower constraints.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: We hope to increase awareness about alternative proteins and encourage greater acceptance, so that the alternative protein industry can become a viable alternative food production capability to enhance our food resilience.

sections.label: Malay speech on food motion
sections.summary: The Motion urges the Government to strengthen food resilience and reduce food waste through whole-of-society collaboration amid geopolitical and climate risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: (In Malay): Mr Speaker, in this Motion, we urge the Government to strengthen food resilience and support efforts to reduce food waste through whole-of-society collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: The move is aimed at ensuring that Singaporeans continue to have access to affordable food amid geopolitical uncertainty and climate-related risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: We have heard many insightful proposals, including those on supporting local farming, improving supply chain resilience, reducing food waste, producing alternative proteins and keeping hawker food affordable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Singapore's food future will not be secured by one solution alone.

sections.label: Food resilience built today
sections.summary: Food resilience is shaped by today's choices and actions, not only during a crisis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Food resilience is not built only during a crisis; it is shaped by the choices and actions we take today.
